# Results — Study 393 (AI-Datacenter-Basket)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The "AI build-out basket" (NVDA,
VRT, ETN, CEG, VST, SMCI, ANET, DELL), equal-weight, monthly-rebalanced, raced against the market
(SPY) and the tech tape (QQQ), and against an equal-weight basket of the same datacenter/power
candidate field. We split the claim in two: is the outperformance a **stable, forward-tradable
theme tilt**, or a **selected, look-ahead concentration bet** — these eight named* because *they
already won? Offline & deterministic from the cache; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce
every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance monthly **total return** (auto-adjusted closes, public, no key) |
| Window | **2022-02 → 2026-05** (52 complete months; ≈ 4.3 years — the generative-AI era) |
| Field | **30** datacenter/power candidates kept: the headline 8 + 22 also-rans (AMD, AVGO, MU, AMAT, LRCX, HPE, CSCO, EMR, PWR, HUBB, JCI, CARR, NRG, NEE, D, SO, DUK, AEP, EXC, EQIX, DLR, AMT) |
| Benchmarks | SPY (market) & QQQ (tech tape), total-return proxies |
| Panel fingerprint | `7d69ca333d53` |

> **Scope caveats (named on the axes).** *Signal* — both the field **and** the eight-name
> membership are **current-membership projected back** (look-ahead): the eight are nameable only
> *because* we already know 2022-2026, and the field excludes any candidate that delisted
> (survivorship — JNPR, absorbed by HPE, drops out). The window starts **2022-02** because the
> merchant-power names CEG/VST are post-spin tickers with no earlier history; that is the AI-era
> window, but it is **one short regime** (≈4.3 years, a single AI capex bull). *Tradability* — a
> 2019 (or early-2022) investor could not have named these eight; the placebo below shows how much
> of the "edge" is hindsight.

## Half 1 — the AI-era spread is REAL on the tape

Equal-weight, monthly-rebalanced; CAGR / annualised Sharpe / max drawdown over the 52 months.

| basket | CAGR | Sharpe | max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **AI-datacenter basket (named 8)** | **71.7%** | **1.65** | −21.7% |
| S&P 500 (SPY) | 14.3% | 0.91 | −20.2% |
| Nasdaq-100 (QQQ) | 18.5% | 0.91 | −26.1% |
| Equal-weight field (1/N of all 30) | 38.8% | 1.55 | −16.7% |
| Basket, net of 10 bps one-way costs | 71.5% | — | — |

HAC (Newey-West) t-stat of the monthly spread:

| spread | mean | HAC t | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Basket − SPY | **+47.1%/yr** | **3.19** | 52 |
| Basket − QQQ | +42.5%/yr | 3.12 | 52 |
| Basket − equal-weight field | +26.0%/yr | 2.37 | 52 |

The spread clears `t ≥ 2` on the real tape — even against the *tech* tape (QQQ, t = 3.12) and even
*after* stripping the "datacenter stuff went up" theme beta (the equal-field control, t = 2.37).
So on the realised AI-era tape the eight genuinely out-earned, and it is not *only* market or tech
beta. **The recent outperformance is real on this short, single-regime tape.**

## Half 2 — but it is selection-after-the-fact (the look-ahead placebo)

The basket's *selection rule*, made explicit: with the **full sample in view**, pick the eight
**highest-realised-return** names of the field and hold them. This is pure look-ahead — and it
manufactures an even larger spread:

| selection rule | CAGR spread vs SPY |
|---|--:|
| **AI-datacenter basket (the famous eight)** | **+57.4%/yr** |
| Ex-post "pick the 8 winners" (look-ahead) | **+69.4%/yr** |
| Random *blind* 8-basket (mean / median of 2,000 seeded draws) | +23.8% / +23.6% /yr |

- The hindsight winners are `VRT, MU, SMCI, NVDA, AVGO, DELL, VST, PWR` — **five of the eight**,
  plus MU, AVGO and PWR (and *missing* ETN, CEG, ANET). The headline basket is ~5/8 of the ex-post
  top-of-the-pile, i.e. it largely *is* the winners-known-in-hindsight basket.
- The ex-post selection rule alone reproduces **121%** of the basket's CAGR spread — selection is
  not *part* of the edge, it is the whole edge (and then some).
- The basket sits at the **100th percentile** of 2,000 random 8-baskets from the same field — *no*
  random draw beat it. But note the field was itself a furnace: a *blindly* chosen eight from this
  same datacenter/power universe still beat SPY by **+23.8%/yr** on average. So the +57% basket
  spread decomposes as ≈ **+24%/yr "the field was hot" (survivorship of the candidate set)** plus
  ≈ **+33%/yr "we hand-picked the top of it" (name selection)** — and **none** of it is a tilt you
  could have named forward.

## Is it one or two names? — single-name decomposition

HAC t of each member's monthly excess over SPY (is the "basket" really a couple of stars?):

| name | mean excess / yr | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|
| VRT | +69.4% | 2.59 |
| ANET | +31.9% | 2.38 |
| CEG | +38.3% | 2.18 |
| NVDA | +48.2% | 2.17 |
| VST | +43.4% | 2.04 |
| SMCI | +84.6% | 1.67 |
| DELL | +48.9% | 1.51 |
| ETN | +12.5% | 1.27 |

Unlike the GLP-1 basket (which was *all* one stock), here the strength is genuinely spread across
several names (VRT, ANET, CEG, NVDA, VST all clear t = 2 individually). That makes the *theme beta*
real — and makes the **selection** the decisive critique rather than single-name concentration: it
isn't one lucky stock, it's a hand-picked top slice of a field that was, in hindsight, on fire.

## Synthetic positive control — selection manufactures a spread on a NO-EDGE tape

A deterministic monthly panel (fixed seed, 84 months × 31 names) where a *pre-named* basket carries
an ``alpha_spread`` and everyone else is identical. The pre-named basket is the honest factor; the
ex-post "pick the winners" rule is the placebo.

| tape | pre-named basket spread (t) | ex-post placebo spread |
|---|--:|--:|
| `alpha = 0.000` (NO true edge) | +4.5%/yr (t = +1.71) | **+14.3%/yr** |
| `alpha = 0.012` (real pre-named edge) | +17.5%/yr (t = +5.77) | +21.0%/yr |

The null row is decisive: with **zero** true cross-sectional edge, a forward-nameable basket has
**no significant** spread (t = 1.71, below the t ≥ 2 bar — luck), yet the look-ahead "pick the
winners" rule still conjures **+14.3%/yr** out of pure selection. That +14.3% is the size of the
artefact a thematic label carries by construction. The engine is faithful: it finds a spread
*only* where one is planted (pre-named, t = 5.77) and manufactures one *whenever* you select on
the outcome (ex-post).

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** The basket-minus-SPY spread is real on the realised AI-era tape (+47.1%/yr,
  HAC **t = 3.19**, n = 52; t = 3.12 even vs QQQ, t = 2.37 even vs the equal-weight field), and the
  strength is spread across several names (VRT, ANET, CEG, NVDA, VST each t ≈ 2). But the basket is
  **selected after the fact**: the synthetic null shows selection alone manufactures a large spread
  with *no* true edge, the ex-post "pick the winners" rule reproduces 121% of the spread, and the
  eight sit at the 100th percentile of random baskets from the same (already-hot) field. Real
  recent spread, **look-ahead / survivorship selected**, one short regime — a `WEAK` going-forward
  case dressed in a strong in-sample t. Hence `MIXED`.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Costs are trivial (an 8-name monthly basket; net CAGR is unchanged to
  the decimal). The mirage is not friction — it is that **you could not have named these eight in
  2019**. The forward-tradable object is a *blindly* chosen eight from the field (~+24%/yr here —
  but only because the candidate field itself is a survivorship-selected hot sector) or a
  pre-specified theme tilt (which the null shows can be zero and insignificant). The +57%/yr is a
  number only hindsight can buy.
- **Ride the build-out by buying the basket? — BUSTED.** "Hold the datacenter-and-power names that
  already won" is not a strategy; it is a label applied to the realised top of the field. The
  build-out being real does not make *this* basket forward-harvestable — picking eight names today
  and holding gets you the random-basket distribution, and even the *theme-beta* portion is the
  field's own survivorship, not a tilt you specified in advance.

> **One-line.** The AI build-out is real, and the eight-name basket genuinely beat the market and
> tech on the AI-era tape (HAC t ≈ 3) — but it is the tape that *named* the basket: strip the
> hindsight and the +57%/yr decomposes into a hot candidate field (≈+24%/yr survivorship) plus
> hand-picking its winners (≈+33%/yr selection), neither of which a 2019 investor could have
> specified, and a synthetic null reproduces +14%/yr of "edge" from selection on a no-edge tape.
